newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly higher but gains pared.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly higher but gains pared.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed higher after posting a new contract high in February before best levels were pared at the close, traders said.
February live cattle ran up to a new high of 66.250 cents per lb before closing at 65.975, up 0.400 cent. Other months finished 0.275 higher to 0.050 lower.

Commercials were on both sides of the market, selling early and then covering on the rally before hedging again at the close. Strength developed in futures when feedlots held firm on their asking prices and packers started to raise bids for cash cattle, traders said.
Demand also developed on further gains in boxed beef values. Increased short covering then boosted futures into buy stops, especially at the old contract high, they said.

Feedlots have no reason to lower asking prices in light of short supplies of well finished cattle and recent weather problems that have cut weight gains. The majority of feedlot cattle need extra days on feed, they added.
R.J. O'Brien and Refco turned buyer along with Smith Barney and ABN Chicogo Corp. Cargill spread long April/short February, thought to be the last of the "Goldman roll", pit sources said.
In live cattle options, RBH sold February 65 to 67 calls and commercials bought 68 calls early. Commercials bought 65 and 66 calls and sold 64 puts late, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of live cattle and rallied late after being pressured early by a rally in corn futures.
A higher CME feeder cattle index added to support. Thinly-traded deferred months posted new contract highs on the late advance, traders said.
ADM Investor Services, Refco and LIT division of First Options notably sold early before buying by Lind Waldock and local short covering rallied prices, pit sources said.
The latest index was up $0.46 at $68.33 per cwt. The index has risen nearly $4 since the first of the year and is at its highest level since March 20, 1995.
Feeder cattle futures closed 0.075 cent per lb lower to 0.400 higher with only January off and March up 0.050 at 68.500 cents. Thinly-traded August through November set new contract highs.
